 What will be the outcome of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board probe into Jensen Huang?
 
 Click here to take the poll and don't forget to share your thoughts in the WSB comments section . 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Cooperation? CoreWeave ( CRWV ) reaches out to Texas governor-elect on data centers . 

 New report: Leaked records point to nearly 400,000 Russian war deaths in Ukraine.

 Real bots: The humanoid race heats up after Agility Robotics ( AGLT ) begins to trade.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Holding the helm 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 After losing nearly half a trillion dollars in market value during the tech wreck on Thursday, Nvidia ( NVDA ) pared some of those losses in the subsequent session. Renewed selling pressure is coming back this morning, with shares down over 5% to $176 in premarket trade. However, this time around is not because of widespread AI fears, but rather internal turmoil happening at the company.

 Spy probe: On Sunday night, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted he had an affair, with reports pointing to a woman named Alice Huang. The two are not related, but the latter is a business executive whom U.S. officials reportedly identified as working for Chinese intelligence. Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, formerly worked as a television reporter in China before becoming an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that operates facilities housing computer systems.

The New York Times , which broke the story of the alleged intelligence effort, reported that Megaspeed purchased more than $4.8B in Nvidia chips over two years. The company also continued selling to Megaspeed after the newspaper disclosed a Commerce Department investigation into whether the customer was helping move restricted AI chips into China. The disclosures add a national security dimension to the debate over Nvidia's access to China, a potential source of chip sales. Huang has advocated allowing exports of earlier generations of advanced AI chips while withholding the newest technology.  Bulls vs. Bears: NVIDIA sparks valuation debate as stock nears six-month low 

 What's next? Nvidia ( NVDA ) has formed a committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, to oversee an investigation. Huang will remain chief executive during the probe, and it's unlikely that he will step down, especially with support coming in from the investing world and American political leadership. That is, as long as he can prove he was duped, and barring some serious developments, like withholding important information from directors or misleading the board. Another alternative might see Huang resign as CEO but transition into an executive chairman role to keep his engineering and AI roadmap intact while retaining his grip on the helm of the company. ( 4 comments )
